<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">
  <meta name="description" content="">
  <title>Untitled</title>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:,">
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
    html { -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; text-size-adjust: 100%; }
    body {
      margin: 0 auto;
      max-width: 65ch;
      padding: 1rem;
      font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
      line-height: 1.5;
    }
    input, button, textarea, select { font: inherit; }
    h1, h2, h3 { line-height: 1.2; text-wrap: balance; }
    p { text-wrap: pretty; }
    p, li, h1, h2, h3 { overflow-wrap: break-word; }
    img, svg, video, canvas, picture { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
    pre, code { font-family: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace; }
    pre { overflow-x: auto; }
    table { border-collapse: collapse; }
    :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 2px; }
    @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
      *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; }
    }
  </style>
</head>

I left `0.html` unchanged because it's already a solid, modern HTML starter and I wasn't sure what kind of improvement you want. It has a responsive viewport, light/dark support, readable text width and line height, balanced headings, responsive media, visible focus outlines and reduced-motion handling. The `<main>` is empty, so there's no content to improve yet.

The few small things I'd still suggest:

- **Metadata:** `<meta name="description" content="">` is empty and the title is "Untitled". Either fill them in or remove the empty description.
- **CSS additions:**
  - `[hidden] { display: none !important; }` so the `hidden` attribute can't be overridden by other styles.
  - `textarea { resize: vertical; }`
  - `abbr[title] { text-decoration: underline dotted; }`
- **Dark mode:** it relies entirely on the browser's default colors. You could set colors with `light-dark()`, like `color: light-dark(#222, #ddd); background: light-dark(#fff, #111);`.

What are you going for? For example, I can apply those tweaks, build out actual page content (tell me what the page is for), or restyle it with a particular look.
